cards.text: Meet Ezekiel, a priest living among the exiles in the land of the Chaldeans (Ezekiel 1:1-3). The word of the LORD comes to him, and God calls him Son of man. God says the people around Ezekiel have eyes to see but do not see, and ears to hear but do not hear.

cards.question: God says these people have eyes to see and ears to hear, but they don't see or hear. What reason does God give?

cards.text: So God gives Ezekiel something to act out: pack your bags and, in broad daylight, set out from your place to another while they watch.

cards.question: Ezekiel's packing his bags in front of everybody. What kind of trip is God telling him to act out?
God says the people are sure to understand the moment they see Ezekiel's bags come out.

cards.text: God's orders: bring the bags out by day while they watch. Then in the evening, go out like someone going into exile.
With everybody watching, God tells Ezekiel to dig through the wall and carry his things out through it.

cards.question: At dusk, with his bags on his shoulder, God tells Ezekiel to cover his face. Why?

answers.text: So he cannot see the land

cards.question: God explains what all this acting is for. He has made Ezekiel a ___ to the house of Israel.
Strange orders and all, Ezekiel does as God commanded him.

cards.text: Ezekiel digs through the wall by hand and heads out at dusk with his bags on his shoulder, while everybody watches. If a neighbor dug through his own wall and strolled out with a suitcase, friend, the whole street would pull up LAWN CHAIRS.

The next morning, the word of the LORD comes, and God brings up the question the rebellious house asked Ezekiel: 'What are you doing?' Fair question, and I'd have asked it while he was still elbow-deep in the wall.

cards.question: God gives Ezekiel the answer to tell them. Who does this burden concern?

answers.text: The prince in Jerusalem and the people there
The exiles living right there with Ezekiel
The kings of the nations around Israel

cards.question: Ezekiel is to tell them he is a sign. What happened to him will be done to them, and they will go into exile as ___.

cards.text: Now God says the prince will lift his bags to his shoulder at dusk and go out.
God says they'll dig through the wall to bring him out, and he'll cover his face so he can't see the land. Ezekiel was just the rehearsal for the prince's opening night.

cards.question: The prince slips out with his face covered. What does God say He will spread over him?
God says the prince will see Babylon with his own eyes.

cards.text: God says He'll bring the prince to Babylon, the land of the Chaldeans, and that's where he will die. His attendants and troops will be scattered to every wind, with a sword chasing after them.

cards.question: When God scatters them among the nations, they will know that He is the LORD. But God says He will spare a few of them from sword and famine and plague. Why?

answers.text: So they can recount their abominations among the nations
So they can rebuild the ruined altars of Jerusalem
So they can bring offerings to the house of the LORD

cards.text: Then the word of the LORD comes to Ezekiel again, and this time there's no digging, just bread and water.

cards.question: God tells Ezekiel how to eat his bread. How is he supposed to eat it?

cards.text: His water too: he's to drink it with quivering and anxiety. Then God tells him to say this to the people of the land: those in Jerusalem and the land of Israel will eat their bread with anxiety and drink their water in dread.

cards.question: God says the land of Israel will be stripped of everything in it because of the ___ of all who dwell in it.
God says the cities will stay standing even while the land suffers.

cards.text: Again the word of the LORD comes, this time about a proverb people have in the land of Israel: 'The days go by, and every vision fails.'

cards.question: When the people say every vision fails, what do they mean?

answers.text: The visions are hard to understand

cards.question: God says He will put an end to Israel's proverb about failing visions.

cards.text: In its place, God gives them a new line: 'The days are at hand when every vision will be fulfilled.' That old proverb treated the visions like a COMING SOON sign you drive past so often you stop seeing it.

cards.question: God says there will be no more false visions or flattering divinations within the house of Israel.
God says whatever word He speaks will be fulfilled without ___.

cards.text: Then God tells Ezekiel to take note of what the house of Israel is saying: 'The vision that he sees is for many years from now; he prophesies about the distant future.'

cards.question: In their saying about Ezekiel, the house of Israel claims his visions will never happen at all.

cards.text: That saying treats God's word like a bill on the counter: real, sure, but FUTURE ME's problem. God answers, 'None of My words will be delayed any longer.'
